findings.quote: there is NO grace period — the request is executed by the next cron tick (every 5 minutes on Vercel Pro), and the schema has no cancel flag
findings.problem: The whole 6.3a prompt (Goal, Inputs, Build 4/5/6/7/8, Constraints, Verify, Finish, done_when) still implements immediate, irreversible deletion. Orchestrator decision 15 (2026-09-07) overrides this: `request_account_deletion()` archives the account immediately (reason `deletion_request`), records `scheduled_for = requested_at + ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS (30)`, `srv_process_account_deletions()` processes only rows whose `scheduled_for` has passed, and the user (sign in → "Keep my account") or a super admin can cancel. The notes field says "REVISE PER ORCHESTRATOR DECISION 15" but the prompt was never revised.
findings.fix: Rewrite 6.3a around decision 15. Inputs: describe `account_deletion_requests (user_id pk, requested_at, scheduled_for, processed_at)` and the archival columns on the per-user table (`archived_at timestamptz`, `archived_by uuid`, `archive_reason 'user'|'deletion_request'|'admin'`), client RPCs `request_account_deletion()` (archives now, sets `scheduled_for`) and `deactivate_account()`, service RPCs `srv_archive_account(user_id, reason)` / `srv_restore_account(user_id)`, and `srv_process_account_deletions()` gated on `scheduled_for <= now()`; state that these ship in `9999_init.sql` via the G2/G3 fixers when the ledger shows 9999 unpasted, otherwise 6.3a writes them in the next free `999x_*` migration (both cases must be in the prompt). Replace every 'processed within minutes / cannot be undone' sentence with the 30-day window and the cancel path. Add `ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS = 30` as a documented constant in `@church/domain` (e.g. `limits.ts`) and list the chosen names in open_issues.

findings.quote: Any signed-in person can request account deletion on the web at `/account/delete` … and in the Anacast app from the More tab
findings.problem: Decision 15 makes **Deactivate account** the self-service action (archive, reversible, signs out) with Delete kept only because Google Play requires it. 6.3a builds no Deactivate path anywhere: no `deactivate_account()` call, no Deactivate row on `(tabs)/more.tsx`, no Deactivate action on `/account`, no "Restore my account" / "Keep my account" flow at sign-in, and no super-admin restore/cancel/initiate controls in `/admin` (users list → Archived → Restore). 6.4 and 6.5 in the same file already expect "Deactivate and Delete rows on More", so the group is internally inconsistent.
findings.fix: Add to Build: (a) web `/account` gets a "Deactivate account" action (Server Action → `deactivate_account()` with the user client → sign out) and `/account/delete` keeps the Play path; (b) mobile More tab gets both rows and a `app/account/deactivate.tsx` (or one screen with two actions) calling `deactivate_account()` then `signOutEverywhere()`; (c) sign-in on web and mobile detects an archived account and offers "Restore my account" (recommended default) and, for a pending deletion, "Keep my account" (deletes the request row and restores); (d) `/admin` users list gains an Archived filter with Restore, Cancel deletion and Start deletion (super admin, service client via `srv_restore_account` / `srv_archive_account` in a `(super)` Server Action after `requireSuperAdmin()`); (e) UI copy per decision 15: "Deactivate account — hides you from your church and signs you out; your data is kept so an administrator can restore you later" vs "Delete account — permanently deletes your account and data after 30 days unless you cancel", both in `deletion-copy.ts` (web + mobile mirror).

findings.quote: `srv_process_account_deletions()` returns the number processed, removes the `auth.users` rows … and returns 0 on a second run
findings.problem: done_when item 1 and Build 1 make `11_account_deletion.sql` assert that a request is executed on the very next `srv_process_account_deletions()` call ("returns 2"). Under decision 15 the first call must return 0 (the row's `scheduled_for` is 30 days out) and the account must already be archived; the test must also cover restore/cancel and that archived users are invisible to the `app.*` membership helpers, audiences and the directory.
findings.fix: Rewrite the RLS test spec: after `request_account_deletion()` assert the account is archived (`archived_at` set, `archive_reason = 'deletion_request'`, push_devices deleted, `my_context()`/`srv_audience_user_ids` exclude the user, `directory_persons` no longer lists them), `srv_process_account_deletions()` → 0; then `update account_deletion_requests set scheduled_for = now() - interval '1 day'` as owner → returns 1 and the auth user is gone; `deactivate_account()` + `srv_restore_account()` round-trip restores memberships/permissions/directory visibility; cancelling a pending deletion (delete the request row / the cancel RPC) restores the account; last-manager audit row as before. Update done_when 1 and the cron unit test accordingly.

findings.quote: processed automatically by the next maintenance run, normally within minutes; the request cannot be undone once processed
findings.problem: The deletion copy (Build 4/5), the privacy 'Your choices' section (Build 6), `docs/PLAY_DATA_SAFETY.md` (Build 7), `docs/ACCEPTANCE_WEB.md` and the Verify curl (`curl … /api/cron/tick … the auth user is gone`) all describe immediate deletion. Decision 15 requires the privacy policy, the Data Safety worksheet and the App Store answers to describe both paths (deactivate vs delete) and the 30-day window; Google's reviewers read exactly this paragraph, and 6.6's `legal.test.ts` will compare it word for word.
findings.fix: Replace the copy with decision 15's two sentences plus 'what the church keeps'; make the privacy 'Your choices' section and the Data Safety 'Account deletion' answer state both paths and the 30-day window; change the acceptance script to: request → account archived and signed out → `select scheduled_for from account_deletion_requests` shows +30 days → cancel via "Keep my account" restores → (optional) set `scheduled_for` in the past in the SQL editor → cron tick → user gone. Update the Verify manual check the same way.

findings.quote: No new migration: the RPC, the table and the cron already exist.
findings.problem: Decision 15 says the archival schema/RPCs/policies/tests are added to the G2/G3 prompts (1.2–1.4) because `9999_init.sql` is not pasted anywhere, and that 6.3a must state both cases (unpasted → nothing to migrate; pasted → 6.3a ships the schema in the next free `999x_*` migration). The current constraint forbids a migration outright and the Inputs/Ledger line says 'no migration is expected'.
findings.fix: Replace the constraint with: 'Read the HANDOFF ledger. If `9999_init.sql` is NOT pasted, the archival columns, `deactivate_account()`, `srv_archive_account`, `srv_restore_account`, the `scheduled_for` column and the archived-user behaviour of the `app.*` helpers are already in 9999 (steps 1.2–1.4) — verify they exist, do not duplicate them. If 9999 IS pasted, write them in the next free descending migration (`9996_account_archival.sql` unless the ledger says otherwise), re-runnable per docs/MIGRATIONS.md, and add the founder paste to-do.' Add the standing local DB verification sequence to Verify in both cases.

findings.quote: Decisions — routes `/account`, `/account/delete`, `/account/deleted`, the confirmation word `DELETE`, "no grace period — processed by the next cron tick" (propose a `cancel_account_deletion()` RPC + 7-day grace as a later step if I want one)
findings.problem: Finish block, notes and two open_issues entries ('Product gap for the founder … proposed as 6.7', 'The 6.2a note … together with the proposed 6.7 cancel RPC') still describe the superseded 7-day-grace proposal; decision 15 absorbed it and renumbered the ops view to 6.7.
findings.fix: Delete the 'no grace period' Decisions line and the two outdated open_issues entries; record instead '30-day grace (`ACCOUNT_DELETION_GRACE_DAYS`), cancel via sign-in or /admin, deactivate = archive' as the decision, and rewrite the 6.3a notes paragraph to match.

findings.quote: `SEC-09` column-level: `authenticated` lacks `select` on `persons.birthdate`, `persons.user_id` (read the exact revoked column list from 1.4b/`docs/RLS.md`) and on `households.hide_from_*` if 1.4b revoked them
findings.problem: PLAN §5 / DESIGN §1 item 3 define the column-level revoke as exactly `persons.birthdate` and `households.anniversary`; `persons.user_id` and the household privacy flags are readable base columns (visibility is handled by the `directory_*` views). Listing `user_id` as an expected revoke could make the audit FAIL and the agent 'fix' it with a migration.
findings.fix: Change SEC-09 to: '`authenticated` has no `select` privilege on `persons.birthdate` and `households.anniversary` (PLAN §5); print any further column 1.4b revoked per `docs/RLS.md` but assert only these two.'

findings.quote: `SEC-12` `account_deletion_requests` has no delete policy.
findings.problem: Under decision 15 a pending deletion is cancelled 'by deleting the request row and restoring the account' (user via sign-in, or super admin). Depending on how the G2/G3 fixers implement it (own-row delete policy vs an RPC), this check may legitimately FAIL, and the audit script would then push the agent to remove a correct policy or 'fix' it by migration.
findings.fix: Reword SEC-12 to: '`account_deletion_requests` has no `update`/`delete` policy for `authenticated` beyond the own-row cancel path 1.4b chose (read `docs/RLS.md`); `anon` has nothing; `service_role` may update/delete.' Add a companion check `SEC-13` (or fold into SEC-12) that archived users (`archived_at is not null`) are excluded by `app.member_org_ids()` / `srv_audience_user_ids` — the decision-15 invariant.

findings.quote: account deletion works

findings.fix: Rename the row 'account deactivation, restore and 30-day deletion work' and cite `11_account_deletion.sql` (6.3a) plus the acceptance curl.
